oneLiner: Peak-cycle memory printing 85% gross margins on an AI-driven DRAM/HBM shortage, at a 5-6x forward P/E that is either the cheapest large cap in tech or a classic cycle-top value trap.
thesis: One of three companies able to manufacture leading-edge DRAM at scale; HBM4 qualified into NVIDIA-class platforms with >$1B already shipped.
HBM fully sold out for calendar 2026 under multi-year fixed-price contracts; management can fill only half to two-thirds of demand and sees the HBM TAM crossing $100B in 2027.
Q3 FY2026 revenue $41.5B (vs $9.3B a year earlier) with 85% gross margin and $18.3B quarterly FCF: earnings power without precedent in memory history.
The whole question is durability: fixed-price HBM converts cyclical pricing into quasi-backlog, but conventional DRAM spot is up 90%+ QoQ, which never lasts.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 FY2026 (ended May 28, 2026; reported Jun 24, 2026)
points: Revenue $41.46B, ~+346% YoY; GAAP gross margin 84.6%; operating margin 80.4%.
Non-GAAP EPS $25.11 vs ~$20.49 consensus; adjusted FCF $18.3B.
Guide: Q4 FY2026 revenue $50.0B plus or minus $1B, gross margin ~86%, EPS $31.00 plus or minus $1.
DRAM $31.3B (76% of revenue); cloud memory BU $13.8B; ~$100B of long-term customer agreements referenced.
HBM sold out for 2026; >$1B HBM4 shipped; targets HBM share equal to overall DRAM share.

segments: DRAM ~76% of revenue, NAND ~24%. By BU: cloud memory $13.8B, core data center $11.5B, mobile/client $11.5B, auto/embedded $4.6B.
HBM is the strategic prize: HBM4 ramping now, HBM4E in 2027.
competitive: HBM share contested: SK Hynix leads (~55-62% in 2026 trackers); sources conflict on whether Micron has overtaken Samsung (high-teens to ~20% vs 5-10% depending on tracker).
NVIDIA's provisional HBM4 allocation: SK Hynix mid-50s%, Samsung mid-20s%, Micron ~20%.
NAND: fifth place (~11% share) behind Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia, Sandisk.
CXMT (China) hit 7.6% of global DRAM in Q1 2026 and IPO'd at ~$85B; not yet at the leading edge.
moat: Leading-edge DRAM process capability (1-beta/1-gamma), HBM4 qualification into the dominant AI platform, and multi-year fixed-price contracts that convert spot pricing into backlog. Breadth across HBM, LPDDR, DDR5 and QLC NAND lets wafers chase the highest return.
risks: Peak-cycle earnings: 85% gross margins are unprecedented and mean-reverting; conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026.
Supply response: Samsung and SK Hynix capacity additions land into 2027.
CXMT share gains (7.6% and rising), possible second Beijing fab, reports of Apple testing CXMT chips.
HBM4 execution vs SK Hynix's allocation lead.
Stock already fell >30% from late-June peak on exactly these fears.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 earnings Sept 29, 2026 (guide: $50B revenue, $31 EPS).
HBM4 multi-customer qualifications through H2 2026; HBM4E volume in 2027.
pricedIn: Forward P/E ~5.6-6.0 vs ~30 industry median; the market refuses to capitalize peak earnings. Up ~667% in 52 weeks yet >30% off the high. Debate: single-digit multiple on peak EPS (cycle top, CXMT looming) vs a structural AI-memory shortage with sold-out fixed-price HBM making this cycle's earnings more durable than any before.

scenarios.bear: FY2026 is the peak: DRAM pricing rolls over in 2027 as competitor capacity lands, CXMT floods conventional DRAM, margins compress toward the 50s, EPS halves, and the stock de-rates the way every prior memory cycle ended.
scenarios.base: Q4 hits ~$50B/$31 EPS; calendar-2027 HBM is largely pre-sold at firm prices, cushioning a moderating conventional curve; earnings plateau rather than collapse; the stock holds a trillion-dollar-class cap with cycle-headline volatility.
scenarios.bull: HBM TAM crosses $100B in 2027 with tightness beyond; Micron holds ~20%+ share into HBM4/HBM4E; NAND scarcity adds a second leg; the 5-6x multiple re-rates toward 8-10x as the market accepts a structurally higher earnings floor.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: at ~5.6x forward P/E the market is pricing a memory downcycle, and the reverse DCF quantifies the implied annual earnings decline. Bear = deep downcycle (prior cycles saw EPS halve-plus); bull = the structural-shortage case where earnings hold and grow.
